basis: Complex spastic paraplegia; optic disc pallor in 30-79% and reduced acuity in 3/3 establish ocular dysfunction. Distal amyotrophy is neurogenic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy in 3/3 reflects denervation from the neurologic disease; direct skeletal-muscle disease is not established.

basis: Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; myopia in 3/5 does not establish direct disease-related eye injury. [Report](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-44259-4)

decisions.ocular: none: myopia occurs in 3/5, but the report describes nonsyndromic hearing loss and does not establish myopia as direct ocular involvement of this disease.

basis: Peroxisomal transport metabolic disorders; neurologic degeneration exceeds ~30% across predominant ALD and ACBD5 disease. Hepatic and retinal damage are subtype-dependent.

decisions.neurologic: involved: ALD dominates this umbrella and commonly causes myelopathy or cerebral disease over its course; ACBD5 deficiency also causes neurodegeneration, supporting >30% overall.

basis: Craniofacial/cervical bone dysplasia and severe periodontal destruction define this syndrome. [Case report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7811426/)

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe destruction of the periodontium is a defining feature of craniofaciocervical osteoglyphic dysplasia; gums and tooth-supporting oral tissues are gastrointestinal.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining leukodystrophy and optic degeneration; eye-degenerative ancestry, optic atrophy in 6/6 and visual loss in 80-99% support ocular primary.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic degeneration is a defining component, supported by the eye-degenerative parent, optic atrophy in 6/6 and visual loss in 80-99%.

basis: Muscle dystrophy; conduction disease ~60-80%, cataracts >50%, GI muscle dysmotility >50%. Endocrine/CNS features omitted at cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: persistent swallowing and intestinal dysfunction reflect direct muscle/enteric disease; dysphagia 59%. [Adult cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42556295/)
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: endocrine involvement is variable; independently coded diabetes is excluded. More consistent cardiac, ocular and gastrointestinal dysfunction takes priority at the four-axis cap.

basis: Mediastinal SFT-spectrum mesenchymal soft-tissue tumor; no cardiac or pulmonary origin specified. [Thoracic review](https://doi.org/10.2214/AJR.11.8430)

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the historical pericytic name does not establish vessel-wall origin or vascular damage; this tumor belongs to the fibroblastic solitary-fibrous-tumor spectrum.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: mediastinal mesenchymal soft-tissue sarcoma in the solitary-fibrous-tumor spectrum; connective-tissue origin supports this axis.

basis: Developmental delay 8/8; ankyloglossia 4/7 with feeding difficulties 6/7 supports oral dysfunction; ptosis 2/5 (40%) affects eyelid function. Weakness does not establish myopathy.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis in 2/5 (40%) is impaired eyelid elevation, within the ocular axis; visual loss is not required to establish eyelid dysfunction.

basis: Developmental impairment characterizes pathogenic 4p duplications; skeletal abnormalities vary by duplicated segment and are not established in most patients across this umbrella.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal anomalies occur in some larger duplications, but neither defining skeletal disease nor >=30% direct skeletal dysfunction across the umbrella is established.

basis: Blood/immune defects and ocular albinism define disease; intellectual disability in both reported siblings (2/2); skin omitted at cap. [Report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8042664/)

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular albinism is defining and entails visual dysfunction; retained with mandatory blood and immune axes under the three-primary cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none: cutaneous albinism is defining, but the four-axis cap prioritizes blood, immune, visual and intellectual dysfunction over skin pigment loss.
